newsitem.title: USA: EMU stability pact seen by yr end-Spain econ chief.
newsitem.headline: EMU stability pact seen by yr end-Spain econ chief.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday he believed the European Union would be able to agree on a stability pact by the December EU leaders summit in Dublin.
"There are good reasons for it to be (resolved)," Rato told reporters here. "There are good chances we will be able to complete the job."
He said that all EU nations needed to comply with the Maastricht criteria.

The stock of Spain's debt would not be converted with monetary union, Rato also said. "The stock of debt in national currencies will stay and will start declining, but it will not be converted," he said.
Asked about recent calls to fix currency rates in early 1998 ahead of convergence, Rato said the EU members had not reached a decision on when parities would be fixed.
